newsitem.title: GERMANY: German December M3 growth slows,96 target missed.
newsitem.headline: German December M3 growth slows,96 target missed.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday that growth in German M3 money supply slowed marginally in December, but admitted that M3 expansion had overshot its target for 1996 as a whole.
The central bank said M3 grew at an annualised rate of 7.9 percent in December compared with its level in the final quarter of 1995.
It grew by 8.1 percent in the final quarter of 1996 from the final quarter a year earlier, the measure targeted with the four to seven percent expansion corridor set for 1996.
"In the entire fourth quarter of 1996 (M3 money supply) was 8.1 percent higher than in the fourth quarter 1995," the Bundesbank said.
"The money supply target for 1996, which looked for an expansion of M3 by four to seven percent in this period, was therefore overstepped," it added.
Economists said the main significance of the figure was that continued high growth in M3 in the final month of 1996 meant that the base for next year's target was high.

This meant that, due to statistical effects, M3 growth was likely to look very weak in the early months of 1997, they said. Some believed that these lower growth figures could provide the Bundesbank with an excuse to cut interest rates in coming months.
